articles.title: The Best Mechanical Keyboard for Programmers
articles.excerpt: Layout, switches and connectivity: what really matters when you type code all day.
articles.body:
## Layout first

Most developers do not need a numpad. A tenkeyless or 75% board keeps the mouse closer and your shoulders relaxed.

## Switches

Linear switches are quiet and smooth; tactile switches give feedback without the noise of clicky ones.

## Our picks

The Typeforge TKL is the safe choice, the 75% Wireless is the best for multi-device setups.

articles.title: Ergonomic Desk Setup Guide
articles.excerpt: Five changes that make an eight-hour day at the desk hurt less.
articles.body:
## 1. Screen at eye level

Use a monitor arm so the top edge of the screen is at eye height.

## 2. Neutral wrists

A split keyboard and a vertical mouse keep your wrists straight.

## 3. Take breaks

No gear replaces standing up every hour.

articles.title: Choosing a Monitor for Coding
articles.excerpt: Resolution, size and pixel density explained for people who read text all day.
articles.body:
## Pixel density matters

27" QHD is the sweet spot for price; 27" 4K gives the sharpest text.

## Ultrawide?

Great for side-by-side editors, but check that your laptop can drive 3440 × 1440.

## USB-C

One cable for video, data and charging keeps the desk clean.

articles.title: USB-C Cables Explained
articles.excerpt: Why two cables that look the same can charge and transfer data very differently.
articles.body:
## Same plug, different cable

USB-C is only the connector. Power (60 W vs 240 W) and data speed (USB 2.0 vs 40 Gbps) depend on the cable.

## Rule of thumb

Charging only: a 240 W cable. Docks and fast drives: Thunderbolt 4.

articles.body:

A monitor light bar does more for your image than an expensive webcam.
